title: Social Engineering AI Toolkit
description_short: A multi-module cybersecurity toolkit that demonstrates and detects modern social engineering attacks across biometric impersonation, AI prompt exploitation, and phishing via text and voice.
description_long: This project explores the human side of cyber risk through three connected modules: biometric identity checks with computer vision and hardware, a controlled GenAI lab for prompt injection and jailbreak testing, and a scanner for phishing patterns across email, SMS, and voice. It was built so members could test ideas safely, learn by doing, and present clear security findings.

title: P4sspl01t Ethical Security Tool
description_short: A password-security suite for generation, cracking, breach detection, and entropy analysis.
description_long: Built across weekly workshops, this password-security project combines both attacker and defender perspectives. Members implemented password generation, controlled brute-force and dictionary testing, basic breach checks, entropy scoring, and practical hardening advice. It doubled as a team software project with version control and sprint-style delivery.

title: Game Off 2025: RE & Security Collaboration
description_short: Joint society project: CompSci teams build games; Cybersoc analyses and reverse engineers them.
description_long: This was a cross-society Game Off collaboration where Computer Science and Data Science teams built the games and Cybersoc focused on security review. Our members debugged binaries, checked unsafe code paths, traced control flow, patched smaller defects, and gave practical secure-coding feedback to improve stability.

title: Cybersoc Website Platform
description_short: The official web platform for Cybersoc, built for clarity, accessibility, and maintainability.
description_long: The Cybersoc website is an ongoing infrastructure project and the society's main public platform. It is built with React, Tailwind CSS, and JSON-driven content so committee members can update information quickly. Students use it as a real engineering environment to ship features, fix bugs, and improve UX through normal version-control workflows.
